memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: You must act according to the decisions they give you at the place the Lord will choose. Be careful to do everything they instruct you to do. Act according to whatever they teach you and the decisions they give you. Do not turn aside from what they tell you, to the right or to the left. - Deut 17:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Once the appointed judges and priests gave their ruling, the people were to follow it carefully, not turning aside to the right or to the left. God established this authority for the good ordering of the community. Ignoring their rightful decisions would lead to chaos, with everyone doing what was right in their own eyes.

This was not blind obedience to any human whim. It was submission to authority that God Himself had established to uphold His law. There is a healthy order here. God knew that a community with no respect for godly authority would tear itself apart through endless disputes.

We too are called to honour legitimate authority, in our homes, our churches, and our society, as an expression of trust in the God who ordains order (Rom 13:1). Of course, human authority is not absolute; when it clearly commands us to disobey God, we must obey God rather than men (Acts 5:29). But apart from such cases, a humble willingness to submit to godly leadership guards us from a proud, self-willed spirit. It reflects the humility of Christ Himself, who submitted perfectly to His Father's will. Do you honour the godly authorities God has placed in your life, or do you resist anything that constrains you?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How do you respond to godly authority in your life?
2. Where might pride be making you resist good leadership?
3. How does Christ's own submission encourage you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me honour the godly authorities You have placed over me. Guard me from a proud, self-willed heart. Amen.
